claims.supported_claim: Strong GCHandle binds awaiter lifetime; reverse callback copies borrowed arguments, marks completion and can inline continuation with ordinary exception handling.
limitations: No complete Godot signal-dispatch concurrency proof.
Inline continuation is not the NativeWeave default.

claims.supported_claim: Native one-shot callable holds the awaiter handle and frees it at destruction.
limitations: One-shot alone does not prove NativeWeave-style cross-runtime quiescence.

claims.supported_claim: Managed callable has explicit handle invocation and release.

claims.supported_claim: Managed callbacks propagate backpressure acknowledgements and errors; completion releases the request cookie then queues native disposal to a managed thread; TLS decisions fail closed on ordinary handler exceptions.
limitations: Read source only, not a whole-project safety verdict.

claims.supported_claim: Rust awaits each body notification's oneshot completion; normal on_complete is followed by a request-state completed write, illustrating that notification is not necessarily the end of native stack access.
limitations: Not a claim YAHA is currently unsafe; other ownership and scheduling must be included.
Tokio/hyper internals not read in this task.

claims.supported_claim: Unregister and drain differ; disposal may wait for executing cancellation callbacks, with special handling when disposing from the same callback.
limitations: Native retirement cannot substitute for managed registration drain.

claims.supported_claim: Perform cleanup outside native/cancellation callback scope; synchronous Dispose requests stop. Explicit notification Dispose closes dispatcher admission, discards pending owned payloads, joins active handlers, and successful DisposeAsync requires managed/native/dispatcher drain.
limitations: Thread-affine profile and self-wait diagnostics require concrete implementation tests.

Cross-review clarified setup compensation, callback binding failure and managed dispatcher drain; these additional paths are design obligations, not covered by the current finite model or runtime tests.
